 School budgets, wastewater projects and local option taxes are on Election Day ballots this year
 Vermont Public | 
 By
 Howard Weiss-Tisman 
 Published November 2, 2026 at 5:00 AM EST
 Facebook 
 Bluesky 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 Courtesy 
 The nine towns in the Taconic and Green Regional School District in southwestern Vermont will vote on selling the Sunderland Elementary School to a private developer. The district offered the school to the town but they turned down the offer due to the deteriorating conditions of the building. 
 There will be a lot of attention paid to the competitive race for governor on Election Day.
 But across Vermont communities have included other important votes in their ballots.
 Barre/Montpelier Career Center 
 Voters in the 18 Washington County towns that comprise the Central Vermont Career Center School District will weigh in on an almost $55 million bond to build a new career center. 
 The district says interest in their courses, such as electrical technology, culinary arts and the building trades, is way up.
 Applications have increased, and last year more than 100 students were not able to get into the courses they wanted.
 Voters rejected a more expensive $149 million project last year, which included purchasing land in Barre for a standalone facility.
 District superintendent Jody Emerson said the new proposal would have the district keep the existing career center at Spaulding High School in Barre while adding a new building to the U-32 High School campus in Montpelier.
 Emerson said the new plan was developed after talking with voters throughout the district who rejected the more expensive plan.
 “We took a look at what the feedback said, which was basically that this was too much money, we don’t like the location, and it made sense to put it on one of our sending schools,” Emerson said.
 School Budgets 
 Barre Unified Union School District officials will try for a fourth time to get voters to approve a budget.
 The district has proposed a $56.6 million budget, which is down about $1.2 million from the budget that was rejected in September.
 Barre voters have rejected the school budget three times already.
 Other education related votes on Nov. 3 include a plan to merge three Northeast Kingdom school districts into a new Orleans Central Unified Union School District . It would include Albany, Barton, Brownington, Glover, Irasburg, Westmore and the Village of Orleans.
 And the nine towns in the Taconic and Green Regional School District will vote on selling the shuttered Sunderland Elementary School to a private developer.
 School board chair Jeff Wilson said the district offered the property to the town of Sunderland. But the selectboard declined the offer due to the cost associated with upgrading the aging school building.
 After an open bidding process, Wilson said the property will be sold for $50,000 if voters approve the plan.
 “We had no plans whatsoever that we could determine for reuse or redevelopment,” Wilson said. “The Sunderland Select Board determined that they did not want to obtain it. They saw it more as a liability, and so we are lucky to be getting $50,000 for it.”
 Local taxes, spending, etc. 
 Along with education ballot measures, a number of towns are also voting on enacting a 1% local option tax.
 The towns of Bennington, Essex and Hinesburg will vote on whether to approve a 1% local option tax. Royalton is voting on allowing cannabis retail sales in town.
 And in Harwick, Vergennes, Whitingham, Bennington, Hartland and Bethel, voters will weigh in on multimillion dollar bond votes for public works projects.
 Williston is voting a third time on its library, after a previous $14.5 million project was rejected.
 The new price tag of about $9 million is scaled back as supporters seek approval for the project.
 And finally, Bradford voters will decide on whether or not the town should amend its charter to allow the recall of elected officers.
 About a dozen Vermont towns have a similar provision that allows citizens to gather signatures and then hold a vote to remove an elected officer.
 Underhill removed a selectboard member in 2021, and Bradford resident Marcey Carver said she wants her town to have a similar option.
 “If there is somebody who is simply not doing their job there’s nothing that a Bradford voter can do,” Carver said. “This is at least a way to hold people responsible.”
